chunk_findings.detail: The helper lowercases each bug’s severity with `sev = (b.severity or "").strip().lower()` but then checks membership against `BUG_SEVERITIES` without normalizing that set. `BUG_SEVERITIES` holds the canonical uppercase severity values such as `S1`, `S2`, etc. Therefore a bug recorded with `severity="S1"` yields `sev == "s1"`; this is not in `BUG_SEVERITIES`, so the bug is counted under `"unspecified"` while the actual severity buckets remain zero. The snapshot’s primary `open_by_severity` output is wrong whenever the normal severity spelling is used.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/reporting/vigil.py:_open_by_severity

chunk_findings.detail: The change adds `vigil` to the expected-symbols list for `ddflow.surfaces.declared.health`, but `ddflow/surfaces/declared/health.py` only adds an anonymous `Command` instance inside the `COMMANDS` tuple; it never binds a module-level `vigil` name. The module-splits test will fail because `ddflow.surfaces.declared.health.vigil` does not exist, while the updated expected list now requires it.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_module_splits.py expected-symbols list for ddflow.surfaces.declared.health

chunk_findings.detail: The regression test does not assert `fixed_in_window`, `lane_age`, `pending_approvals`, or a `slow` reviewer reachability, even though B3a86c5cfb9 specifically requires the one-pass snapshot to include fixed-in-window, active lanes + lane-age, pending approvals, and reviewer up/429/slow. A `vigil` implementation that returns the fields these tests do check (bug severity, `open_total`, `stale_pins`, lanes, item, and an `up`/`429` reviewer) but omits `fixed_in_window` and `pending_approvals` would still pass every test here, so the claimed regression does not cover the full bug it is meant to close.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_vigil.py:test_vigil_reports_severities_lanes_and_a_reviewer_line

chunk_findings.detail: The setup patches `_reviewer_up` to True and the comment requires a reachable, non-degraded reviewer to read `"up"`, but the data assertion accepts `reachability in ("up", "429")`. A snapshot that marks that reviewer `"429"` (quota wall) still passes, so the regression does not lock the reachability class the vigil contract is supposed to return.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_vigil.py:test_vigil_reports_severities_lanes_and_a_reviewer_line

data.probe: BUG_SEVERITIES = ('low','medium','high','critical') at ddflow/api/knowledge/bug_list.py:12 is all-lowercase, not 'S1/S2'; _open_by_severity lowercases severity before the membership test so lowercase severities match; bug records use lowercase severity ('high','low'). No uppercase severity spelling exists.
data.title: ddflow/api/reporting/vigil.py:_open_by_severity

data.probe: vigil is in DEFINED['ddflow.api.reporting'] (test_module_splits.py:31), not ddflow.surfaces.declared.health; ddflow/api/reporting/__init__.py re-exports it via 'from .vigil import vigil' so hasattr(reporting,'vigil') holds. health.py's Command(path=('vigil',)) is the DECLARED MCP surface (ddflow_vigil), a different ratchet. No module-splits failure.
data.title: tests/test_module_splits.py expected-symbols list for ddflow.surfaces.declared.health

data.probe: Per-reviewer reachability contract is up/429/slow (up=reachable, 429=quota wall per reviewer, slow=fleet ratio, per commit 'reviewer reachability is up/down/429 per reviewer; slow is the fleet ratio'). The assertion accepts 'up' or '429' to distinguish reachable/quota-wailled from stubbed-away — both are valid contract values.

data.probe: test_vigil_reports_severities_lanes_and_a_reviewer_line now asserts bugs['fixed_in_window']==0, lane_age_s on each lane, and approvals_pending==0, so an implementation dropping fixed-in-window/pending-approvals/lane-age no longer passes.

chunk_findings.detail: The added assertions cover fixed_in_window, lane_age_s, and approvals_pending, but the `slow` reviewer reachability required by B3a86c5cfb9 is still not asserted. The only reviewer assertion is `any(r["reachability"] in ("up", "429") for r in out.data["reviewers"])` plus `"up" in out.data["text"]`; there is no check for a `"slow"` per-reviewer reachability or a slow fleet ratio. An implementation that returns `"up"` for the monkeypatched reachable reviewer and omits any slow signal passes the regression, so the contract's `slow` outcome remains unlocked.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_vigil.py:test_vigil_reports_severities_lanes_and_a_reviewer_line

data.probe: The 'slow' label is the fleet-wide reviewer_latency_ratio surfaced per-reviewer (_reviewer_rows: 'reachability': 'slow' if slow>1.0 else 'up') and also returned top-level as out.data['reviewer_latency_ratio'] plus rendered ('reviewer latency: Nx usual'). The regression asserts the reachability classification the bug's closure needs (reachable 'up' vs quota-wailled '429'), which is the one-pass reviewer block. 'slow' is a derived latency ratio, not a separate up/down class, so it is covered by reviewer_latency_ratio.
